title: The Ghost Orchid
tagline: The rarest flower in the garden vanished from a locked glasshouse. The door remembers every card. The cards don't always remember their owners.
briefing: Hartwell's Ghost Orchid is a pale, leafless flower that blooms for only a few days a year. Collectors would pay a fortune for it.
On Thursday at 6:30 am the head of security found its pot empty in Glasshouse 3. The orchid had been cut cleanly out of its bark.

Glasshouse 3 can only be opened with a staff key card, and every card swipe is logged. The garden's gates, car park and patrols keep logs too. The thief is hiding in plain sight, somewhere in these records.
rules: Glasshouse 3's door locks itself and opens only with a staff key card. There is no other way in: the glass roof and walls are alarmed and nothing was triggered.
After 9:00 pm the only ways in or out of the garden are the car park barrier (vehicles) and the North Gate (pedestrians). Both are logged.

suspects.name: Iris Tan
suspects.description: Has cared for the Ghost Orchid for six years.
suspects.motive: Was refused permission to take a cutting for her own research.
suspects.statement: I did the evening misting from six to twenty to seven, then paperwork in my office, and drove home at about twenty to ten.

suspects.name: Theo Grant
suspects.description: Joined the garden a year ago. Cycles to work on sunny days, drives when it rains.
suspects.motive: Bank statements show heavy debts. An email on his phone from an overseas 'plant enthusiast' asks about 'the pale one'.
suspects.statement: I checked the seed trays in Glasshouse 3 from quarter past nine and drove straight home at half past. I was in bed by eleven.

suspects.name: Malik Haddad
suspects.description: Works late running long experiments in the lab block.
suspects.motive: Has complained that the Ghost Orchid gets more funding than his lab.
suspects.statement: I was in the lab from half ten until quarter to twelve, watching a machine run. Then I drove home.

suspects.name: Ezra Booth
suspects.description: Walks a patrol round all night, scanning checkpoint tags as he goes. Took the 10 pm photo of the orchid.
suspects.motive: Has a master card and knows the site better than anyone.
suspects.statement: I did my rounds like always. The orchid was there at ten. I've got the photo.

evidence.title: Glasshouse 3 door log
body: Card numbers are listed in the staff register. Card #331 belongs to Florence Kerr, head gardener.

evidence.title: Patrol photo
body: 22:00. Glasshouse 3, through the glass from outside: the Ghost Orchid in flower in its pot.

evidence.title: Florence Kerr, head gardener
body: “I lost my key card on Tuesday at lunch. I think I left it on my table in the staff canteen. I reported it to security that afternoon but it hadn't been cancelled yet.”
“On Wednesday night I was at my sister's wedding in Dunmore, 200 kilometres away. I was dancing till one in the morning, there are a hundred photos.”

evidence.title: North Gate (pedestrians)
body: No pedestrian entries or exits between 21:00 and 06:00, apart from Ezra's patrol scan at 23:04.

evidence.title: Ezra's patrol checkpoints
body: Site map note: walking from the North Gate to Glasshouse 3 takes 8 minutes. Car Park B is next to the North Gate.

evidence.title: Lab block door
evidence.source: Key card system. The lab block has one door.
body: Card #262 (Malik Haddad): In 22:30, Out 23:45. No other entries or exits.

evidence.title: Canteen cook
body: “Tuesday lunchtime, after Florence left, the young chap from propagation sat at her table. I saw him pick up a card off it and put it in his pocket. I thought he'd hand it in.”
Lost property book: nothing handed in on Tuesday or Wednesday.

questions.prompt: During which visit to Glasshouse 3 was the orchid stolen?
questions.explanation: The patrol photo shows the orchid still there at 22:00. The only entry after that is card #331 at 23:05.

questions.prompt: Card #331 is Florence's. Why couldn't she have used it?

options.text: She lost it on Tuesday and was 200 km away at a wedding on Wednesday night
Head gardeners don't go into Glasshouse 3

questions.explanation: She reported it lost on Tuesday (it wasn't cancelled yet, which is why it still worked) and has a hundred wedding photos as an alibi.

questions.prompt: Which suspect lied about when they left the garden?
questions.explanation: Theo says he drove home at 21:30, but the barrier camera shows his car leaving at 23:20, eight minutes after card #331 left Glasshouse 3.

questions.prompt: Ezra was on site all night. Why couldn't he have used the card at 23:05?

options.text: He took the 22:00 photo, so he must be honest
He scanned the North Gate at 23:04, 8 minutes' walk from Glasshouse 3, and Car Park B at 23:10
His master card would have shown in the log

questions.explanation: At 23:04 he was at the North Gate. The earliest he could reach Glasshouse 3 is 23:12, and at 23:10 he was scanning Car Park B beside the gate.

Iris drove out at 21:40 and nobody came back in. Malik was inside the one-door lab from 22:30 to 23:45. Ezra was at the North Gate. Theo was still on site, lied about leaving, and was seen pocketing Florence's lost card.

solution.summary: On Tuesday Theo Grant pocketed Florence's lost key card in the canteen. On Wednesday he swiped into Glasshouse 3 with his own card at 21:15 to look normal, then hid in his car until the garden was quiet. At 23:05 he used Florence's card to get back in, cut out the Ghost Orchid and drove out at 23:20. He told the police he'd left at half past nine. The number-plate camera disagrees.

chain.step: The orchid was there at 22:00, and the only entry after that is card #331 at 23:05 to 23:12.
Card #331 is Florence's, lost on Tuesday. She was 200 km away.
No one entered the site after 20:00 or 21:00, so the thief was already inside.
Iris left at 21:40. Malik was in the one-door lab. Ezra was at the North Gate at 23:04 and Car Park B at 23:10.
Theo's car left at 23:20 although he claims 21:30, and he was seen pocketing Florence's card.

eliminations.why: Her car left at 21:40, and no vehicle or pedestrian came back in.
The lab block has one door and his card shows him inside from 22:30 to 23:45.
Scanned the North Gate at 23:04 and Car Park B at 23:10. Glasshouse 3 is 8 minutes' walk away.

playtest.solvePath: The case rewards building one timeline from five logs. Most solvers pin the theft to 23:05 quickly, then go hunting for who was still on site. Theo's 23:20 exit is the moment it clicks.
pitfalls: Testers suspected Ezra immediately (master card, took the photo). His checkpoint scans now rule him out with a walking time.
Some wondered if Iris drove out and walked back in. The North Gate log rules that out.
Some asked if the thief could have climbed in through the glass. The rules now say the glass is alarmed and nothing triggered.
revisions: Added the North Gate pedestrian log so 'left by car, came back on foot' is closed.
Gave Ezra a Car Park B scan at 23:10 as well as the North Gate, so he can't be argued into the glasshouse with a sprint.
Added the canteen cook so there's positive proof Theo had Florence's card, not only that he had the chance.
